notes: Import outcomes must account for all 791 normalized records, and the graph must represent all 24 supplied source documents, using SourceDocument or a documented equivalent.
Citation page and section keys may be null when the locator type does not provide that dimension; passage_id is the canonical citation target.
Evidence-bearing edges require non-empty source_refs and extraction provenance. Structural or system-generated edges may use documented system provenance and empty source_refs.
Six questions produce seven answer/trace records because P3 requires vector and graph modes.
P3 evidence_text is limited to 6000 characters per mode; document how the implementation counts characters.
Evidence-bearing Assertion nodes must also retain actor, version, created_at and review_state.
Logical fields may be inherited from an explicit enclosing run/scope record when equivalent structures are documented; do not repeat metadata needlessly.
Preserve the input passage ID if re-chunking; map every derived chunk back to its parent passage for citations and retrieval evaluation.
A public shared-corpus partition is not a tenant authorization mechanism. Production design must distinguish shared public evidence from confidential scopes.
The P3 character cap includes every source-derived summary/graph description sent to generation and is counted in Unicode code points.
Saved per-case evaluation results must deterministically reproduce aggregate scores without additional model calls. Candidate-authored labels remain provisional.

Use the supplied graph core as a reference, not a fixed ontology. You may modify, merge, or replace its node and relationship types; document consequential choices and map your representation to the required evidence provenance, tenant/project isolation, source-version identity, assertion state, and human-review state. Equivalent representations are acceptable. Every source must still have an inspectable document representation, even if you rename SourceDocument. Do not treat the listed type names as a checklist.

Automatically extracted assertions and relationships default to unreviewed. A model call or automated validation is not human review. Keep this independent of the regulatory state reported in the source: an accepted proposal or a reviewer conclusion may still be an unreviewed extraction. Human review and correction are production-design topics only; no working review operation or UI is required. Explain who can review/correct an extraction, what provenance is retained, and how an approved correction would reach indexes and later answers.

Preserve inspectable old source records, assertions/graph exports, and the answers and traces generated before an update, connected by source, snapshot, index and run identifiers. Files are sufficient. No old-version or as-of retrieval/generation interface is required. Current source versions may still describe historical proposals: source revision state and the chronology described by a source are separate.
Seven main answer/trace records remain in results/answers.jsonl and results/traces.jsonl. The three behavior-fixture answers/traces use results/fixtures/ and never count as FDA answers.

Source-correction stages are before and after; conflict stage is combined. Each fixture answer/trace also carries scenario_id, stage and run_id. The report lists commands, actual checks/failures, and file paths connecting preserved sources/graphs to before/after runs. Equivalent enclosing metadata is acceptable.
Fixture history artifacts must include both correction stages. Fixture outputs describe candidate execution; supplied behavior-cases.json is an input contract, not a run result.
Unreviewed extractions may be used in this prototype; their status must remain visible in the graph export. Do not claim a human approval that did not occur.
